documents.title: Optometry diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Diabetic eye examination, date of exam 01/12/2023.
Patient: Hailey Roy. Referring: primary care.
History: type 1 diabetes. No visual complaints.
VA cc 20/20 OD, 20/20 OS. IOP 15/16. Pupils normal, no APD.
Dilated fundus exam: clear media, cup-to-disc 0.3 both eyes, macula flat with good foveal reflex, vessels normal caliber, no hemorrhages, exudates or neovascularization OU.
Impression: diabetes without diabetic retinopathy either eye.
Recommend annual dilated exam. Thank you for the referral.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: DM1 f/u. Has been better about checking before meals since December, misses the bedtime check most nights. Fasting mostly 140-190 on her log. No lows below 70 this quarter. Eye exam done in January, report received, no retinopathy.

O: vitals as charted. Alert, well. Feet: sensation intact to monofilament, pulses normal.

A/P:
DM1 - modest improvement on her log. A1c and BMP today. Same glargine and lispro scale. Reviewed sick-day basics: never skip basal insulin, check more often when ill.
Hypothyroid - stable, TSH at physical.
Pneumococcal vaccine indicated with diabetes: PCV20 given today, one and done.
Physical in September.

documents.title: A1c result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c came down a little from December. Still above where we'd like, but the direction is right and your kidney and salt levels are fine. Keep doing what you're doing with the pre-meal checks.

documents.title: No-show
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt did not arrive for 3:40 appt. Called, no answer, left VM to reschedule. Texted the scheduling link.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Apologized for missing the 7th, mandatory overtime at work that week. Over her lunch break today.

Sugars: no meter today, reports mornings "mostly in the 150s". Says her pharmacy flagged that the glargine pens may need a new approval when her plan renews next month.

Exam brief: well, BP fine, feet intact.

Plan: no lab today (A1c at physical in September). Will watch for the PA request from pharmacy and handle it. Refills sent for 90 days of both insulins and levothyroxine.

documents.title: Prior authorization - insulin glargine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Fax from pharmacy: Medicaid requires renewed PA for insulin glargine pens for new benefit year. PA form completed with dx type 1 DM, current dose 24 units qHS, duration of therapy since childhood. Submitted through the plan portal. Approval received 7/13, valid 12 months. Pharmacy notified, pt texted that pens are ready.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 31F.

Interval: no ER visits, no new meds. Works days at the call center, walks the dog evenings. Sleep OK. Mood good. PHQ-2 0.

Diabetes: checks 3x daily most days. No severe lows. Still no endocrinologist; prefers to keep it here.
Thyroid: no symptoms.

Meds: glargine 24u qhs, lispro scale with meals, levothyroxine 88 mcg, prenatal MVI. NKDA.
Prevention: Pap 2021 normal, next due 2024. Pneumococcal done March. Flu/COVID next month at nurse visit. Tdap 2019.

Exam: Well-appearing. HEENT normal, TMs clear, oropharynx with tonsils surgically absent. Neck supple, thyroid normal size, no nodules. Heart regular rate, no murmurs. Lungs clear to auscultation. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin: injection sites clean. Ext without edema. Diabetic foot exam: normal skin and nails, monofilament 10/10 sites bilaterally, pulses intact. Neuro grossly normal.

A/P: healthy 31yo with long-standing DM1 above goal and hypothyroidism.
- Fasting labs today: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, TSH, urine microalbumin.
- Continue current regimen pending A1c.
- Annual eye exam due January.
Return in 3 months.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hailey - everything from the physical is normal except the A1c, which is a little lower than March but still well above goal. Thyroid, kidneys, cholesterol and blood counts all fine. Nothing to change today; we'll look at your meter together in December and see where the highs are coming from.

documents.title: RE: Physical labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: ok thanks. will bring the meter

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu IM L deltoid and 2023-24 COVID vaccine IM R deltoid. Screening questions negative. Tolerated both. Watched 15 minutes, no reaction.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from her car on lunch break; she consented to a video visit and confirmed her date of birth.

Uploaded meter download beforehand. 14-day average about 185. Highest readings late evening after dinner. Fasting 130-170. One reading of 66 before lunch, treated.

No symptoms. Taking everything.

A: DM1, persistently above goal, evening pattern.
P: Talked through carb counting at dinner and using the full correction on the scale rather than half of it, which she admits she does to avoid lows. No dose change to glargine. In-person with A1c in February. Eye exam due next month.
